en.title: Rested Bruins host a banged-up Panthers side on a back-to-back

Bruins: James Hagens went on injured reserve with a back injury after a cross-check on Thursday and is expected to miss multiple weeks. Matthew Poitras is day-to-day.
Boston last played on Thursday, a 6-2 win in Pittsburgh. Florida is on the second night of a back-to-back.
Projected goalies: Jeremy Swayman for Boston, Jacob Markstrom for Florida.
records: The Panthers are 0-3 against Atlantic Division opponents this season. The Bruins have played only one division game, a 4-1 loss to Ottawa on Oct. 5.
Brady Tkachuk leads Florida with 10 goals in his first season there. Matthew Tkachuk has 25 points, 21 of them assists.
David Pastrnak leads Boston with 22 points. The Bruins allow just 2.35 goals a game.
The last 11 meetings averaged 6.3 goals. Florida won the last one, 2-1 in Boston on April 2.
betting: Market: Bruins 1.75, Panthers 2.12, about 55–45 without the margin. The model says 55–45 too, so there is no real disagreement.

en.title: Eichel faces his old club as Vegas closes a five-game road trip
en.deck: Vegas is 11-5-2 and has won two straight on a trip that ends in Buffalo. The Sabres come off their most convincing win of the season, 5-2 over Columbus. The market calls it even; the model leans Vegas.
news: Reports point to a goalie change on both sides: Adin Hill for Vegas after Carter Hart stopped 25 of 26 on Thursday, and Colten Ellis for Buffalo.
Sabres out: Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk, plus goalie Alex Lyon. Ryan McLeod and Louis Crevier were scratched last game.
Josh Norris scored twice against Columbus, and Conor Timmins made his season debut.
Golden Knights: Parker Wotherspoon (upper body) remains on injured reserve.
records: Jack Eichel has six goals and three assists in seven games against the team that drafted him.
Zach Benson has a six-game point streak and leads Buffalo with 13 assists, but has only two goals. The model flags him as due.
Buffalo has won the last three meetings and both of its afternoon games this season.
Vegas has the league's seventh-best power play at 27.8%. Buffalo's penalty kill ranks 27th at 69.6%.
betting: Market: 1.92 on both sides, a straight 50–50. The model has Vegas at 54%, a clear lean the market does not share. The model assumes Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen in Buffalo's net, while reports expect Ellis.
Total: the market prices over 5.5 at 1.61 (about 59%). The model says 55%, and the last six meetings averaged 5.7 goals, so the model sits on the lower side.

en.title: Vladar returns to Calgary with the Flyers last in the East
en.deck: Philadelphia is 4-10-4 and blew a late lead in New York on Thursday. Calgary let a 3-1 lead slip against Anaheim on Friday. Two teams that have lost their grip on third periods meet in a near coin flip.
news: Dan Vladar is projected to start against the club he played for from 2021 to 2025. He is 3-4-2 with a 3.21 GAA and .883 save percentage.

Flyers: Rasmus Ristolainen and Nikita Grebenkin are on injured reserve, and Jett Luchanko is expected to miss time.
records: The Flyers went winless in their first nine, then won three straight, and have one win in their last six.
The Flames lost their first five, then won five straight at home. They have one win in their last four.
Calgary's power play sits in the top five at 30%, helped by Zayne Parekh. Rookie William Stromgren has two goals in three games since his call-up.
Only 39% of Philadelphia's games have gone over 5.5 goals. Calgary beat the Flyers in Philadelphia last month.
